igneous.cooling-rate.text: Magma that cools slowly underground grows big crystals. Lava that cools fast at the surface has tiny crystals or none.
igneous.cooling-rate.fieldNote: Slow cooling = big crystals. Fast cooling = tiny or none.

pumice.gas-bubbles.text: Pumice is frothy lava that cooled fast. The holes are gas bubbles that got trapped. It is so light it floats on water.
pumice.gas-bubbles.fieldNote: Pumice: full of gas-bubble holes, floats.

obsidian.volcanic-glass.text: Obsidian is volcanic glass. The lava cooled so fast that no crystals had time to grow at all.

basalt.lava-rock.text: Basalt is the most common volcanic rock on Earth. It forms when runny lava cools quickly. Most of Iceland is made of it.
basalt.lava-rock.fieldNote: Basalt: dark lava rock. Most of Iceland is made of it.

map.grid-references.text: A grid reference names one square on a map: the letter across first, then the number down.
map.grid-references.fieldNote: Grid reference: letter across, then number down.

map.compass-north.text: A compass needle points north. Most maps are drawn with north at the top, so you can turn the map to match the ground.
map.compass-north.fieldNote: Compass points north. Maps put north at the top.
